gap: No result ChatGPT got states how fast a 1.5V lithium AA actually wears out: Gough Lui ran the XTAR 4150mWh AA through 100 lab cycles and measured a loss of 0.85–0.89 mWh per cycle, which projects to 80% of its energy at about 843 cycles against XTAR's 1,200-cycle rating, with only about 63% of the charging energy coming back out.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited rivals I could open. Charge-Test (Michael Barton, 2026-10-05) measured usable energy at 0.1/0.4/1 A but says outright that its results don't show which battery lasts longest over hundreds of cycles, and it leaves service life out of the ranking. Light And Matter (Matthew Gore, 2026-10-24) measured EBL capacity and flash recycle times but has no cycle data. Techtest.org (the same author's German 15-cell comparison) and best-batteries.com (rated specs and a 'for guidance only' table) have no cycle-wear measurements either. I could not read the Digital Camera World pages; only their titles loaded. ChatGPT's own answer said 'long-term durability wasn't established.'
decides: It backs XTAR 4150mWh as the best value pick, and that is the cell Dealectric already lists (xtar-1-5v-aa-4150mwh-8-pack). It is the only candidate with a published cycle-wear measurement, and the projection of about 770–840 cycles to 80% is honest life data, about 30–35% short of the 1,200-cycle claim. The CLR 4300 still leads on energy per charge: Charge-Test measured 3,703 vs 3,420 mWh, and 3,719 vs 3,297 mWh at 1 A. But nobody has measured its cycle life, so a durability-minded shopper has a measured reason to choose the 4150 at $24.99. Gough Lui's I-V testing also suggests keeping loads below 1.25 A, which matters for flashes and other high-drain devices.
